advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an assertion that criterion_prompt_id('F1', gate_key='code_review') == 'code-review-F1' to cover the documented code-review built-in mapping.
evidence: Docstring documents this case: src/rebar/llm/criteria/ids.py:19 `plan_review built-in  ``F1``           → ``plan-review-F1``` and line 19 for code_review `code_review built-in  ``F1``           → ``code-review-F1```
Tests exercising gate_key='code_review' only use 'project.foo': lines 12 and 25 of tests/unit/test_code_review_project_criteria.py
ABSENCE: no assertion of criterion_prompt_id('F1', gate_key='code_review') anywhere in the new test file — the bare-id (no-dot) equivalence class under the code_review gate is untested.
advisory.finding: The code-review built-in mapping (a bare id under gate_key='code_review', e.g. criterion_prompt_id('F1', gate_key='code_review') == 'code-review-F1') is documented in the module docstring table but has no test. Every test that exercises gate_key='code_review' passes a dotted 'project.foo' id; the no-dot branch under the new gate is never asserted.
scenarios: A regression that mis-prefixed only bare-id code-review criteria (e.g. dropping the prefix for non-project ids under code_review) would pass all current tests.
advisory.suggested_fix: In test_resolver_maps_project_criterion_into_code_review_namespace (or a new test), add: assert criterion_prompt_id('F1', gate_key='code_review') == 'code-review-F1'
